title_en: Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan v. Zhai Xiaoming — patent right dispute
ruling_gist_en: I. Article 148 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall abide by laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association, and owe a duty of loyalty and a duty of diligence to the company. Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall not take advantage of their positions to accept bribes or other illegal income, nor shall they misappropriate company property." Article 153 of the same Law provides: "If any director or senior management personnel violates laws, administrative regulations, or the articles of association and causes damage to the interests of shareholders, the shareholders may file a lawsuit in a people's court." According to the above provisions, where a director, senior management personnel, or controlling shareholder or other person violates laws, administrative regulations, or the articles of association, thereby infringing upon the company's interests, and the company, being under the control of the aforesaid person, is unable or fails to assert its rights in its own name, causing damage to the interests of other shareholders, such other shareholders, in order to protect their own legitimate rights and interests as well as the company's interests, have the right to file a lawsuit in a people's court.

full_text_en:
Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan v. Zhai Xiaoming — dispute over patent rights

Ruling Summary

I. Article 148 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall observe laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association, and owe a duty of loyalty and diligence to the company. Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall not take advantage of their positions to accept bribes or other illegal income, nor shall they misappropriate company property." Article 153 of the same Law provides: "Where directors or senior management personnel violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, thereby harming the interests of shareholders, the shareholders may file a lawsuit with the people's court." Pursuant to the above provisions, where a director, senior management personnel, or controlling shareholder of a company violates laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, thereby infringing upon the company's interests, and the company, being under the control of such person, is unable or fails to assert its rights in its own name, thereby causing harm to the interests of other shareholders, such other shareholders, in order to protect their own legitimate rights and interests as well as the company's interests, have the right to file a lawsuit with the people's court.

II. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, an invention-creation made in the course of performing the duties of an employee, or primarily using the material and technical resources of an employer, is a service invention-creation. The right to apply for a patent for a service invention-creation belongs to the employer.

Plaintiffs: Wu Linxiang, male, 54 years old, shareholder of Changzhou Yi Shi Tong Digital Lock Co., Ltd., residing at Xinminyuan, Tianning District, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff: Chen Huanan, male, 45 years old, shareholder of Changzhou Yi Shi Tong Digital Lock Co., Ltd., residing at Guanhe West Road, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Zhai Xiaoming, male, 55 years old, shareholder and executive director of Changzhou Yi Shi Tong Digital Lock Co., Ltd., residing at Jingzhong Lane, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Changzhou Yi Shi Tong Digital Lock Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Chuangye North District, Science and Technology Park, Xinbei District, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhai Xiaoming, executive director of the company.

Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming and the Third Party Changzhou Yi Shi Tong Digital Lock Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Yi Shi Tong Company") over a dispute concerning patent rights.

The Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan alleged: The Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, was established on April 25, 2003. Both Plaintiffs and the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming are shareholders of Yi Shi Tong Company, and the Defendant also serves as its legal representative. Since its establishment, Yi Shi Tong Company has been engaged in the research and development of the "Yi Shi Tong Digital Intelligent Lock" project. In 2004, Yi Shi Tong Company submitted the project as part of the Changzhou Science and Technology Development Plan. In July 2004, the Changzhou Science and Technology Bureau entered into a *Changzhou Science and Technology Project Contract* with Yi Shi Tong Company, and in September of the same year, the Xinbei District Science and Technology Bureau also entered into a *Science and Technology Project Contract* with Yi Shi Tong Company. The above application materials and science and technology contracts clearly stated that the research content was the Yi Shi Tong digital lock, key, and key setter, and the project leader and principal researchers were all the Defendant. Yi Shi Tong Company invested a substantial amount of funds, equipment, and other material and technical resources in the project, and the technical achievements should belong to Yi Shi Tong Company. The Defendant, in his own name, applied for four patents based on the above technical achievements, including one invention patent and one utility model patent for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Supplied by a Key," as well as two design patents titled "Electronic Key" and "Electronic Key Setting Tool." The Defendant's actions infringed upon Yi Shi Tong Company's right to apply for patents. The Plaintiffs requested the people's court to order the Defendant to bear corresponding legal liability. During the first-instance proceedings, the two Plaintiffs withdrew their claims regarding the right to apply for the two design patents for "Electronic Key" and "Electronic Key Setting Tool." After review, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court approved the withdrawal. The two Plaintiffs ultimately requested a judgment that the right to apply for the invention patent and the utility model patent for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Supplied by a Key" belong to Yi Shi Tong Company, and that the Defendant bear the litigation costs and other reasonable expenses.

The Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan submitted the following evidence:

1. One set each of the invention patent application documents and utility model patent application documents for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Supplied by a Key," for which the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming is the applicant. Used to prove that the Defendant, without authorization, applied for patents in his own name for technical achievements that should belong to the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company.

2. Two pages of enterprise registration information for the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, and one copy of Yi Shi Tong Company's articles of association. Used to prove that the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan and the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming are all shareholders of Yi Shi Tong Company, and the Defendant also serves as its legal representative.

3. One copy of the 2004 Changzhou Science and Technology Development Plan application materials, one copy of the *Changzhou Science and Technology Project Contract* entered into between the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, and the Changzhou Science and Technology Bureau, and one copy of the *Science and Technology Project Contract* entered into between Yi Shi Tong Company and the Xinbei District Science and Technology Bureau of Changzhou. Used to prove that Yi Shi Tong Company is the owner of the technical achievements such as the Yi Shi Tong digital lock, key, and key setter, and is the party to the relevant science and technology project contracts.

4. One copy of the sci-tech project allocation slip for September 2003, one copy each of the sci-tech project allocation application and allocation slip for July 2004, part of the invoices for the purchase of equipment and components from May 2003 to July 2005, three agreements, invoices, and payment vouchers for ordering lock and key molds in July 2003, pay slips, receipts and vouchers for housing, utilities, telecommunications, computers, and automobiles from 2003 to 2005, drawings of the Yi Shi Tong Digital Intelligent Lock, early design drawings and parts lists of the Yi Shi Tong Digital Intelligent Lock, product instructions, certificates of conformity, photographs, and four physical specimens of the Yi Shi Tong digital lock set (electronic lock, key, and setting tool). Used to prove that the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, is the developer of the technologies for the Yi Shi Tong digital lock, key, and key setter.

5. One copy of the testimony of witness Wang Wei, and copies of the *Agreement* held by Zhenjiang Dantu District Xingyu Die-Casting Factory and 11 drawings. Used to prove that on July 18, 2003, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, entered into an *Agreement* with Zhenjiang Dantu District Xingyu Die-Casting Factory, which processed the housing of the electronic lock according to the drawings provided by Yi Shi Tong Company.

6. One copy of the testimony of witness Tang Xinyuan, and copies of the *Agreement* held by Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory and 3 drawings. Used to prove that in July 2003, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, entered into an *Agreement* with Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory, which processed components of the electronic lock according to the drawings provided by Yi Shi Tong Company.

7. One copy of the testimony of witness Chen Jianfeng, and a pay slip for Chen Jianfeng's wages collected by Tao Tao on her behalf. Used to prove that Tao Tao, a witness of the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming, has an interest in this case.

Upon the application of the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court duly summoned witnesses Wang Wei, Tang Xinyuan, and Chen Jianfeng to testify in court. When testifying in court, witness Wang Wei (male, 37 years old, Han ethnicity, factory director of Zhenjiang Dantu District Xingyu Die-Casting Factory) submitted the originals of the Plaintiffs' evidence item 5 and stated: On July 18, 2003, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, entered into an *Agreement* with Zhenjiang Dantu District Xingyu Die-Casting Factory, providing drawings and entrusting Xingyu Die-Casting Factory to process the zinc alloy housing for the keys and locks. As of October 2005, more than 1,000 sets of housing had been processed. The processed housing was identical to the physical exhibits presented by the Plaintiffs in court, and all processed housing had been delivered to Yi Shi Tong Company. At the request of Yi Shi Tong Company, improvements were made to the processed products midway through. When testifying in court, witness Tang Xinyuan (male, 52 years old, factory director of Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory) submitted the originals of the Plaintiffs' evidence item 6 and stated: In July 2003, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, entered into an *Agreement* with Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory, providing drawings and entrusting Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory to process components of the electronic lock. A total of more than 2,000 sets of components were processed over time, and improvements were made to the products at the request of Yi Shi Tong Company midway through. When testifying in court, witness Chen Jianfeng (female, 43 years old) stated: I was employed by the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, to buy groceries, cook, and do laundry for the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming and his witness Tao Tao, with a monthly salary of RMB 500.

Upon the application of the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, on January 9, 2006, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court lawfully obtained evidence from the State Intellectual Property Office. The Office provided certification stating that the patents applied for by the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming in August 2005 include one invention patent and one utility model patent both titled "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Supplied by a Key," and two design patents titled "Electronic Key" and "Electronic Key Setting Tool," with application numbers 2005100414845, 2005200744982, 2005300876718, and 2005300876722, respectively.

The Defendant Zhai Xiaoming argued: The Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan do not have standing as plaintiffs and cannot file this lawsuit in their individual names; the invention-creation involved in this case is not a service invention-creation, and the relevant technical solutions were formed before the establishment of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company. After the Third Party's establishment, it merely implemented the above technical solutions rather than developed or researched them, and the above technical solutions are fully covered by several of the Defendant's earlier patents. Therefore, the right to apply for the patents in question should not belong to the Third Party.

The Defendant Zhai Xiaoming submitted physical exhibits including four electronic keys, two electronic locks, and a circuit board approximately 3 cm in diameter. Used to prove that the Defendant had completed the technical solutions related to the patent applications before the establishment of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, and therefore the Defendant has the right to apply for the patents in question.

The Defendant Zhai Xiaoming applied for witness Tao Tao (male, Han ethnicity, 42 years old, employee of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company) to testify in court. Tao Tao stated: The physical exhibits provided by the Defendant were all samples made from the end of 2000 to 2003, but there were no formal design drawings; I was mainly responsible for the electronic circuits and software aspects of the electronic lock. Regarding the software, the physical exhibits provided by the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan and those provided by the Defendant are in some respects the same and in others different; the differences are in aspects such as the interface.

The Defendant Zhai Xiaoming applied for witness Zhou Tianwen (male, Han ethnicity, 53 years old, employee of Jiangsu Shuguang Optical Electronics Company) to testify in court. Zhou Tianwen stated: From the summer of 2000 to the end of 2002, Zhai Xiaoming repeatedly consulted me about developing an electronic lock product. During this period, I helped him process parts, including lock bolts, key heads, springs, and other parts; I cannot recall the names of other parts, and I do not know where the processed parts were specifically installed. As for the physical evidence presented in court, I do not know how to disassemble it; I probably saw it between 2001 and 2002.

The Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, did not participate in the proceedings and did not submit any evidence.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court lawfully organized the parties to conduct cross-examination of the evidence. After cross-examination, regarding the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan's evidence item 1, the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming argued that its authenticity could not be confirmed due to the lack of the original for verification. The court held that this evidence was the Defendant's patent application documents, and the relevant originals should be in the Defendant's possession. Since the Defendant did not provide contrary evidence, the authenticity of this evidence should be confirmed. Regarding the Plaintiffs' evidence items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7, the Defendant did not raise any objections, so they were confirmed. Regarding the evidence submitted by the Defendant, the Plaintiffs argued that its probative value was insufficient. The court held that the physical evidence submitted by the Defendant could not itself prove the time of its creation. Furthermore, although the Defendant applied for witnesses Tao Tao and Zhou Tianwen to testify in court, due to the existence of an interest relationship between Tao Tao and the Defendant, the probative value of his testimony was low. Although witness Zhou Tianwen testified that he had processed parts for the Defendant, he could not explain the technical solutions involved in the parts he processed. Therefore, none of the evidence submitted by the Defendant could achieve its intended purpose of proof, and it could not prove that the Defendant had completed the technical solutions related to the patent applications before the establishment of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court found the following facts through the first-instance trial:

The Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, was established on April 25, 2003. Its founding shareholders were the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming, and a non-party Li Jiadong. Zhai Xiaoming served as the company's executive director and general manager. Li Jiadong later withdrew, leaving the company's shareholders as Wu Linxiang, Chen Huanan, and Zhai Xiaoming. The company's business scope includes the manufacture and sale of digital intelligent locks and digital intelligent security devices, as well as technical development and technical services for digital intelligent locks, mechatronics, and computer software. On March 1, 2004, Yi Shi Tong Company submitted the "'Yi Shi Tong' Digital Intelligent Lock Project" to the Science and Technology Bureau of Changzhou High-tech Development Zone for inclusion in the "Changzhou Science and Technology Development Plan." The project design task record stated: "The products of this project consist of three independent products: the lock, the key, and the key setter"; "This project research is based on existing electronic locks and fingerprint locks worldwide, including magnetic card electronic locks, IC card electronic locks, IP card electronic locks, TM card electronic locks, and electronic access control systems. This project research is conducted on the basis of inheriting and developing the advantages of existing electronic locks, with significant breakthroughs in key technical issues"; the principal researchers of the project were Zhai Xiaoming, Tao Tao, Wu Linxiang, and You Qiguo. On July 22, 2004, Yi Shi Tong Company entered into a *Changzhou Science and Technology Project Contract* with the Changzhou Science and Technology Bureau for the "'Yi Shi Tong' Digital Lock Project," which involved three products: the lock, the key, and the key setter. On September 21, 2004, Yi Shi Tong Company entered into a *Science and Technology Project Contract* with the Xinbei District Science and Technology Bureau of Changzhou for the "'Yi Shi Tong' Digital Lock Project," which stated that the project leader was Zhai Xiaoming, and the principal researchers were Tao Tao, Wu Linxiang, and You Qiguo. From September 2003 to September 2004, the Changzhou Science and Technology Bureau and the Xinbei District Science and Technology Bureau of Changzhou allocated a total of RMB 400,000 to the "'Yi Shi Tong' Digital Lock Project" in three installments.

From May 2003 to July 2005, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, purchased equipment and components for the above project and entrusted others to process parts. On July 18, 2003, Yi Shi Tong Company entered into an *Agreement* with Zhenjiang Dantu District Xingyu Die-Casting Factory, under which the factory processed the housing of the electronic lock according to the drawings provided by Yi Shi Tong Company; on July 28, 2003, Yi Shi Tong Company entered into an *Agreement* with Changzhou Wujin Minghuang Radio Equipment Factory, under which the factory processed components of the electronic lock according to the drawings provided by Yi Shi Tong Company.

On March 20, 2005, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, submitted an *Application Report* to the Xin District Administration for Industry and Commerce of Changzhou, stating: "Since the company's establishment two years ago, it has invested substantial financial and human resources in developing the 'Yi Shi Tong Digital Intelligent Lock' with independent intellectual property rights. No sales have been achieved during these two years."

On June 22, 2005, the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, entered into a *Lock Purchase and Sale Agreement* with the Yangzhou Civil Air Defense Office, under which the Yangzhou Civil Air Defense Office agreed to purchase Yi Shi Tong digital locks, keys, and managers from Yi Shi Tong Company, including 170 door locks, 65 keys, and 5 managers.

In August 2005, the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming, in his own name, filed with the State Intellectual Property Office one invention patent application and one utility model patent application for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Supplied by a Key," with application numbers 2005100414845 and 2005200744982, respectively. Comparing Zhai Xiaoming's above patent application documents with the drawings provided by the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, which bore the name of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company, the technical solutions recorded in the drawings provided by the Plaintiffs were identical to those in Zhai Xiaoming's patent applications.

Separately, it was also found: The Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan paid RMB 6,000 in patent agency fees for this lawsuit. This fact is evidenced by the patent agency fee invoices issued on December 9, 2005, by Jiangsu Changzhou Xinlian Law Firm and Changzhou Tianlong Patent Agency Co., Ltd., respectively, with the payee being Wu Linxiang.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan are proper plaintiffs in this case; 2. Whether the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming has the right to apply for the patents in question.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held in the first instance:

I. The Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan are proper plaintiffs in this case and have the right to file this lawsuit.

Article 148 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall observe laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association, and owe a duty of loyalty and diligence to the company. Directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel shall not take advantage of their positions to accept bribes or other illegal income, nor shall they misappropriate company property." Article 153 of the Company Law provides: "Where directors or senior management personnel violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, thereby harming the interests of shareholders, the shareholders may file a lawsuit with the people's court." Pursuant to the above provisions, where a director, senior management personnel, or controlling shareholder of a company violates laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, thereby infringing upon the company's interests, and the company, being under the control of such person, is unable or fails to assert its rights in its own name, thereby causing harm to the interests of other shareholders, such other shareholders, in order to protect their own legitimate rights and interests as well as the company's interests, have the right to file a lawsuit with the people's court. In this case, the Plaintiffs Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan and the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming are all shareholders of the Third Party, Yi Shi Tong Company. The Defendant, as the company's executive director and general manager, actually controls the company. The two Plaintiffs contend that the Defendant infringed upon Yi Shi Tong Company's right to apply for patents, and that, under the Defendant's actual control, the company is unable to assert its rights in its own name, thereby harming the company's interests and the two Plaintiffs' shareholder interests. Under these circumstances, the two Plaintiffs filed this lawsuit with the people's court, asserting that the patent technical solutions applied for by the Defendant should belong to Yi Shi Tong Company, and naming Yi Shi Tong Company as a third party. This is in accordance with legal provisions. Therefore, the Defendant's defense that the two Plaintiffs lack standing to sue and are not proper plaintiffs in this case cannot be established and is not accepted.

II. The Defendant Zhai Xiaoming does not have the right to apply for the patents in question.

First, based on the facts of this case, it cannot be determined that the technical solutions of the patent applications in question were completed by the Defendant Zhai Xiaoming individually, nor can it be determined that the technical achievements belong to the Defendant.

Defendant Zhai Xiaoming argued that the patented technology solution was developed by him personally and that the solution was formed before the establishment of the third party, Yishitong Company, which was established merely for industrialization purposes. Zhai Xiaoming provided relevant physical evidence in support of this claim. However, the defendant only submitted the relevant physical products, which could not prove the formation time of the patented technology solution. The witness testimony provided by the defendant also could not prove that the patented technology solution was completed by the defendant personally; therefore, it cannot be determined that the technological achievement belongs to the defendant. The defendant further argued that several of his personal patents granted before the establishment of Yishitong Company had already fully covered the patented technology solution but failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove this. Furthermore, according to the facts of this case, Yishitong Company had not produced a finished "Yishitong Digital Lock" product during the two years following its establishment in April 2003, and it was only in June 2005 that products were placed on the market. This also indicates that during these two years, Yishitong Company was continuously researching and developing the relevant products. Therefore, the defendant's above defenses are untenable and are not adopted.

Secondly, based on the facts of this case, it can be determined that the patented technology solution is a service invention, belonging to the third party, Yishitong Company, with the corresponding patent application right also belonging to that company.

According to Article 6 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law), an invention-creation made by a person in the course of performing his duties for the entity, or mainly by using the material and technical conditions of the entity, is a service invention-creation. The right to apply for a patent for a service invention-creation belongs to the entity. In this case, the plaintiffs, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, provided technical materials such as design drawings of the third party, Yishitong Company. Upon comparison, the technical solution reflected in the above technical materials is identical to the patented technology solution of defendant Zhai Xiaoming, confirming it to be the same technical solution. Since its establishment in 2004, Yishitong Company reported the above technical solution project to the Changzhou Municipal Science and Technology Development Plan Project, with Zhai Xiaoming as the project leader, and researchers including Tao Tao, Wu Linxiang, and You Qiguo from Yishitong Company. Yishitong Company invested considerable human and material resources in the technical solution project, purchased specialized instruments and equipment for the project, and the Changzhou Municipal Science and Technology Bureau also allocated funds to support the project. These facts are sufficient to prove that the patented technology solution was completed by Zhai Xiaoming and others in the course of performing their duties for Yishitong Company and by using the company's material and technical conditions. It constitutes a service invention, and the relevant technological achievements should belong to Yishitong Company, with the right to apply for a patent also belonging to that company. Even further, even if the defendant had independently engaged in research and development of the relevant technical solution before the establishment of Yishitong Company and achieved certain research results, since Yishitong Company formed the final technical solution through further research and development, and Zhai Xiaoming and others performed their duties for the entity and used its material and technical conditions during this process, the final technical solution, i.e., the patented technology solution, should also be determined as a service invention, belonging to Yishitong Company, with the corresponding patent application right also belonging to that company.

In summary, the invention patent and utility model patent for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Powered by a Key" applied for by defendant Zhai Xiaoming in his own name should belong to the third party, Yishitong Company. The plaintiffs, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan's claim that the patent application right for the above technical solution belongs to Yishitong Company has factual basis and legal support and should be upheld. The two plaintiffs also requested an order that the defendant pay other reasonable expenses but failed to submit corresponding evidence; therefore, this claim is not supported.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 22, 2006:

Defendant Zhai Xiaoming's application for the invention patent and utility model patent for "A Micro-power Electronic Lock Powered by a Key" (patent application numbers 2005100414845 and 2005200744982, respectively) in his own name is improper. The patent application right for the above technology belongs to the third party, Yishitong Company.

Zhai Xiaoming appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Jiangsu High People's Court, his main grounds being: 1. The first-instance judgment found the facts unclearly. It improperly determined the technical solution to be a service invention merely based on the identity between the technical solution reflected in the technical materials such as drawings provided by the appellees Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan and the appellant's patented technology solution. The technical materials such as drawings provided by the appellees neither bore the seal of the original third party, Yishitong Company, nor indicated the date of their formation, and the appellees admitted in the first-instance court that all drawings were copies or reprints from a computer. According to the basic rules of civil procedure evidence law and the rigor and logic inherent in inventions themselves, the determination of key issues such as the main features of the technical solution, the comparison of technologies, and the formation time of the technical solution should be based on sufficient and rigorous evidence, not hastily on ambiguous evidence. The first-instance judgment considered that the technical materials such as drawings provided by the appellees were corroborated by witness testimony, but the witnesses provided by the appellees only gave uncertain testimony on the existence of the drawings and did not provide reliable and detailed testimony on key issues such as the details of the technical solution involved in the drawings, the drawers, the drawing time, and the revisions of the technical solution. The above witness testimony also could not prove the formation time, the forming party, or the technology comparison of the patented technology solution. The first-instance judgment's finding that the physical evidence and witness testimony provided by the appellant could not prove that the patented technology solution was formed before the establishment of Yishitong Company was also incorrect. The testimony of witness Zhou Tianwen in court could prove that the patented technology solution was indeed formed before the establishment of Yishitong Company. Furthermore, the main components of the physical evidence are metal materials such as copper and iron. Based on the scientific principle of radiation and decay cycles, the formation time of this physical evidence can be objectively determined through scientific testing methods. The first-instance court should have designated a professional appraisal institution to conduct an appraisal to ascertain the key facts of the case, rather than simply denying the objective attributes and evidentiary value of the physical evidence solely because the evidence itself cannot indicate its formation time. 2. The first-instance judgment's determination that the patented technology solution was a service invention was improper. The appellant had independently completed the main part of the patented technology solution before the establishment of Yishitong Company, basically completing the entire inventive concept and sketches, and making models and some parts. Yishitong Company only provided some assistance during the technical experimentation and implementation phase. This assistance itself did not produce any substantive or creative technical innovation but merely implemented and made minor improvements according to the technical solution already independently completed by the appellant before the establishment of Yishitong Company. The witnesses provided by Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan also admitted this in court. Therefore, the patent application right for the invention should belong to the appellant. The request was to set aside the first-instance judgment and dismiss the claims raised by the two appellees in the first instance.

The appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, did not provide new evidence.

The appellees, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, argued: The purpose of establishing the original third party, Yishitong Company, was precisely to research and develop electronic locks. The patented technology solution is a service invention. The technical solution belongs to Yishitong Company, and the patent application right for it should also belong to Yishitong Company. The original judgment found the facts clearly and the evidence was sufficient. They requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The appellees, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, did not provide new evidence.

Upon second-instance trial, the Jiangsu High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance. Additionally, it found: In March 2004, the original third party, Yishitong Company, reported the "Yishitong Digital Intelligent Lock" project to the Science and Technology Bureau of Changzhou High-tech Development Zone for the "2004 Changzhou Municipal Science and Technology Development Plan." The "Design Task Statement for the Science and Technology Plan Project" in the application materials stated: "This project is exclusively researched, developed, and implemented by Yishitong Company... All intellectual property rights resulting from this project's research are independent intellectual property rights and belong exclusively to Yishitong Company."

The focus of the dispute in the second instance was: Whether the invention-creation in question constitutes a service invention.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held in the second instance:

According to Article 6 of the Patent Law, a service invention refers to an invention-creation made in the course of performing the duties of the entity or mainly by using the material and technical conditions of the entity. The right to apply for a patent for a service invention-creation belongs to the entity.

The appellees, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, argued that the purpose of establishing the original third party, Yishitong Company, was precisely to research and develop the "Yishitong Digital Intelligent Lock" project. The appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, as the executive director of the company and the project leader, collaborated with other company personnel on the research and development of the project. This itself constituted performing the tasks of Yishitong Company. Moreover, the invention-creation was mainly accomplished by using the material and technical conditions of Yishitong Company. Therefore, the invention-creation is a service invention. Zhai Xiaoming argued that the technical solution of the invention-creation was independently completed by him before the establishment of Yishitong Company, and the establishment of Yishitong Company was merely for the implementation of that technical solution. Therefore, the invention-creation is not a service invention. The parties disputed whether the invention-creation constituted a service invention. The key issues in dispute were: first, determining the completion time of the technical solution of the invention-creation. If the completion time was before the establishment of Yishitong Company, then the invention-creation is not a service invention; second, determining the purpose for which Yishitong Company provided the material and technical conditions for the invention-creation. If it was not for completing the invention-creation but merely for verifying or implementing it, then the invention-creation is not a service invention. The court held that, based on the facts of this case, it can be determined that the invention-creation is a service invention.

First, based on the facts of this case, it can be determined that the technical solution of the invention-creation was completed after the establishment of the original third party, Yishitong Company. A rights holder filing a patent application for an invention-creation is one of the signs that the technical solution has been completed. If there is no conclusive evidence to prove that the actual completion time of the relevant technical solution is earlier than the patent application date, only the patent application date can be used as the basis for presuming the completion time of the technical solution. In this case, the appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, filed the patent application for the invention in question in August 2005, while Yishitong Company was established in April 2003. Although Zhai Xiaoming argued that the technical solution of the invention-creation was completed before the establishment of Yishitong Company and provided relevant physical evidence and the testimony of witness Zhou Tianwen, neither piece of evidence sufficiently proves his claim. The main reasons are: 1. The physical evidence itself cannot reflect its formation time. Even if an appraisal were conducted, it could only determine the formation time of the main metal components in the physical evidence, and the formation time of the metal components cannot be equated with the formation time of the physical evidence itself. 2. According to the testimony of witness Zhou Tianwen, Zhou Tianwen merely processed some parts for Zhai Xiaoming, did not know exactly where the processed parts were installed, could not disassemble the physical evidence provided by Zhai Xiaoming, could not confirm whether the physical evidence contained the parts he processed, and could not confirm whether the physical evidence was the product of the invention-creation for which Zhai Xiaoming applied for a patent. Therefore, Zhou Tianwen's testimony cannot corroborate the physical evidence. In conclusion, it can be determined that the technical solution of the invention-creation was completed after the establishment of Yishitong Company. Zhai Xiaoming's appeal ground that the invention-creation was completed by him personally before the establishment of Yishitong Company cannot be sustained and is not adopted.

Secondly, the invention-creation was mainly accomplished by using the material and technical conditions of the original third party, Yishitong Company. The appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, does not deny that Yishitong Company invested substantial human, material, and financial resources in the invention-creation. He merely argues that Yishitong Company's act of providing material and technical conditions did not itself produce any substantive or creative technical innovation but merely implemented and made minor improvements according to the technical solution he had already independently completed before. Therefore, he argues that the invention-creation was not mainly accomplished by using Yishitong Company's material and technical conditions. The appellees, Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, argued that the invention-creation was mainly accomplished by using Yishitong Company's material and technical conditions. The court held that the documents submitted by Yishitong Company to the local Science and Technology Bureau for the "Yishitong Digital Intelligent Lock" technology development plan application, as well as the science and technology project contract and project funding voucher signed with the local Science and Technology Bureau, all indicate that the invention-creation was exclusively researched, developed, and implemented by Yishitong Company, and Zhai Xiaoming was the project's research and development leader. Furthermore, the "Application Report" submitted by Yishitong Company to the Changzhou New District Administration for Industry and Commerce in March 2005 recorded that since its registration and establishment two years prior, the company had invested substantial financial and human resources in developing the "Yishitong Digital Intelligent Lock" with independent intellectual property rights. Based on the above evidence, it can be determined that researching and developing the invention-creation was a primary task of Yishitong Company, and its completion was mainly accomplished by using Yishitong Company's material and technical conditions.

Given that the appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, does not deny that the technical solution reflected in the technical materials such as drawings of the original third party, Yishitong Company, submitted by the appellees Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan, is the same as the patented technology solution he applied for himself, and the identity of the technical solution reflected in the drawings and other technical materials provided by Wu Linxiang and Chen Huanan with Zhai Xiaoming's patented technology solution has no bearing on determining whether the invention-creation is a service invention. The first-instance judgment did not determine the invention-creation to be a service invention solely based on this point. Therefore, Zhai Xiaoming's appeal ground raised on this matter cannot be sustained and is not supported.

In conclusion, it can be determined that the appellant, Zhai Xiaoming, and other researchers of the original third party, Yishitong Company, completed the invention-creation in the course of performing Yishitong Company's tasks and by mainly using the company's material and technical conditions. The invention-creation is a service invention, and the corresponding patent application right belongs to Yishitong Company. The appellant's appeal claim that the invention-creation is his personal invention and the patent application right should belong to him lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 17, 2006:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
